sources.fullCitation: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, vocal by Max Mensing. “Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar.” Slow fox; label credit “Fritz Rotter & Dr. B. Kaper”. Parlophone 80.235, matrix B 38451, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar — Parlophone 80.235
sources.creator: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, mit Gesang: Max Mensing
sources.researchNote: The filmed label identifies Parlophone 80.235, matrix B 38451, Saxophon Orchester Dobbri and Max Mensing. R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 8, printed p. 926, independently lists this song with “B 38451 Dobbri Saxophon Orch.” Its general year 1930 does not specify a session or issue date. The Berlin session in 1930 and the description of the copy as a French issue remain uploader-supplied; neither is printed on the label. The examined label does not name Wiener Boheme-Verlag; the publisher credit is supported by separate sources.

sources.title: Otto Dobrindt — Wikipedia (German)
sources.creator: Wikipedia contributors
sources.researchNote: Records that he joined Carl Lindström AG in 1924 as a recording manager and became its chief recording manager, and that from 1925 he issued his own productions under pseudonyms including Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri, Odeon Tanz-Orchester, Wiener Bohème-Orchester, Dobbri, Robert Renard, Eddie Saxon, Frank Sandlers, Eric Harden and Götz Höhne; his orchestra accompanied Ufa stars on record, among them Hans Albers. These statements follow the secondary Wikipedia article rather than an examination of the original recordings.

sources.shortCitation: Parlophon B 4502, “Gib nur acht, über Nacht kommt die Liebe”
sources.fullCitation: Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri, with Max Mensing singing. “Gib nur acht, über Nacht kommt die Liebe.” Valse Boston; label credits Dr. B. Kaper. Parlophon B 4502, printed number 38185, n.d. Label photograph and audio transfer published by Musicaviennensis on YouTube, 1 May 2016.
sources.title: Gib nur acht, über Nacht kommt die Liebe — Parlophon B 4502
sources.creator: Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri; Max Mensing; Musicaviennensis (uploader)
sources.researchNote: The label shown at the start of the video identifies Parlophon B 4502, prints the number 38185 and names Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri, singer Max Mensing and Dr. B. Kaper. The number 38185 is not treated here as an independently verified matrix or take. The uploader reports a Berlin recording in January 1930; the label does not establish its date or the manufacture date of the photographed copy. The structured date is the YouTube publication date. The label and upload describe the German song W-S008, not the Polish-language version.

works.publicNote: A signed manuscript of the song in the Kaper Papers is dated Berlin 1927, three years before the Vienna edition registered in Hofmeisters Monatsbericht and the United States registration of 1930.

contributions.scopeNote: The displayed Parlophon B 4502 label names Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri and Max Mensing. It prints 38185 but does not establish an exact recording date or take; the January 1930 date is supplied by the uploader.
Named on the Parlophone label as “Saxophon Orchester Dobbri”, with Max Mensing singing.
